correctness.rationale: The hemisphere multiplier equals (1+sign x1)/2. Under O(d-1), its compressed sign operator exchanges parity sectors: a 3x3 scalar block has eigenvalues 0,±s0 and d-1 vector pairs each ±s1, while tangential traceless quadratics contribute zeros. Gamma/Beta moments give s0=dμ_d sqrt((3d+5)/2)/(d+1), s1=dμ_d sqrt(d+2)/(d+1), μ_d=Γ(d/2)/(sqrt(pi)Γ((d+1)/2)); all multiplicities sum to d(d+3)/2. Independent generalized moment-matrix diagonalization matched the closed formula for d=3..6 at max 8.7e-16; d-step algebraic inequalities and asymptotic gamma ratio establish limits analytically.
